But when they had tied him up, Paul said to the centurion standing by, "Is it legal for you to fogg a Roman citizen who is unconddemned?" When the centurion heard this, he went to the tribune and reported, "What are you about to do? This man is a Roman citizen." The tribune asked Paul, "Are you a Roman citizen?" Paul replied, "Yes." The tribune said, "I paid a large sum for my citizenship." Immediately those who were about to examine him withdrew. The tribune was also afraid.

Alan, can you read please? When we came into Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself with the soldiers guarding him. Three days later, he called together local Jewish leaders and said, "Brothers, though I had done nothing against our people or customs, yet I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans." The Romans wanted to release him because there were no grounds for the death penalty. But when the Jews objected, Paul was compelled to appeal to the emperor even though he had no charges against his nation.

This is really interesting. Before, Paul said he wanted to return to Rome to face judgment from the emperor. Now, he says the Jews attacked him and if he wanted to, he could complain to the emperor and bring charges against them. He asked to speak with these leaders because it was for the sake of the hope of Israel that he was bound with this chain.

They replied, "We have received no reports about you from Judah or any brothers here who spoke ill of you. But we would like to hear your thoughts." For with regard to this sect, they knew it was spoken against everywhere.

After setting a date to meet, the Jewish leaders came in great numbers to his residence.
